rationale: This is the archive's `maturity_wall_funding_adequacy` with the financing leg's WINSOR swapped for RANK — a purely monotone re-normalization of the same variable and the same conditioning weight, i.e. exactly the cosmetic variant the objective warns against rather than a diagnosed economic improvement.

Changing the near-term obligation denominator from dlc to lct is a genuine economic change (debt maturities vs. all current claims) with a real stability motivation, though it is still a close relative of the archive signal and confounds the denominator change with the rank re-normalization.

The archive has already tested equity-tilted financing under distress twice (`distress_equity_tilted_financing_mix`, `debt_overhang_equity_infusion`) and both delivered the opposite of the positive sign asserted here, and a raw sstk-scaled issuance measure is largely a rediscovery of the share-issuance anomaly with its sign flipped.

This is the most economically complete version of the adequacy idea and pairs it with a genuinely different distress dimension, but the ratio risks being dominated by che/dlc (a standard liquidity ratio) rather than by the financing-flow content the hypothesis emphasizes.

Identical construction to the archive's `borrowing_without_tax_shield` apart from replacing WINSOR with RANK on the financing leg; the diagnosis of tail-driven FMB slopes is plausible but the proposal admits it "changes only the statistical representation," which is a cosmetic re-test, not a new mechanism.

Internally consistent (rising wcap plus weak operating cash flow scaled against net borrowing, negative sign follows naturally) and it introduces a conditioning state absent from the archive, but the working-capital-growth leg overlaps heavily with the well-documented accruals and asset-growth anomalies, so the incremental content is uncertain.
